module purpose: neorv32_cpu is a CPU wrapper that connects frontend, control, counters, register file, ALU, LSU, PMP and optional ICC sub-units, forwards the instruction and data bus interfaces, and locally forms the machine-interrupt vector, the combined xCSR read-data bus, the register-file write-back value, and the PMP fault signal.

use-case flows.value: debug-interrupt request delivered from the module boundary to the control block
fast-interrupt request vector delivered from the module boundary to the control block
machine software/external/timer interrupt request vector assembled and delivered to the control block
combined xCSR read-data value from ALU, counters, PMP and ICC sources, with disabled sources forced to zero
register-file write-back value combined from ALU result, load/store read data, CSR read data and return-PC data, then delivered to the register file
PMP access-fault decision delivered to control and LSU, or forced low when PMP support is disabled

conceptual assets.concept: Debug-interrupt request entering the control path
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow is the direct delivery of dbi_i to the control sub-unit at line 266 through the connection to formal irq_dbg_i. Integrity is Established because the consumer in the unsupplied control block must receive exactly that request value for the flow the connection defines; there is no local transformation or storage in this wrapper.

conceptual assets.concept: Fast-interrupt request vector entering the control path
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow is the direct delivery of firq_i to the control sub-unit at line 268 through the connection to formal irq_fast_i. Integrity is Established because the control consumer must receive exactly the fast-interrupt vector presented at this module boundary; this wrapper only passes the value into the consumer.

conceptual assets.concept: Machine interrupt request vector assembled from timer, external and software interrupt inputs
conceptual assets.reasoning: Line 276 computes irq_machine from the three external interrupt inputs by concatenation, and line 267 passes that vector to the control sub-unit as irq_machine_i. Integrity is Established because the control consumer must receive the exact three-bit interrupt indication defined by line 276; corrupting any source bit or the computed vector changes the interrupt request seen by control. Availability is also Established combinationally while the input levels are present because this wrapper does not gate or store the vector.

conceptual assets.concept: Combined xCSR read-data value presented to the control block
conceptual assets.reasoning: Line 279 defines xcsr_res as the bitwise OR of xcsr_cnt, xcsr_alu, xcsr_pmp and xcsr_icc, and line 264 delivers that combined value to the control sub-unit as xcsr_rdata_i. The contributing sources come either from sub-unit outputs (lines 299, 371, 416, 445) or are forced to zero when their feature is disabled (lines 305, 426, 454). Integrity is Established because the control consumer must receive exactly the combined CSR data value defined by these lines; a wrong value would make the CSR read path incorrect. Availability is Established under the RTL-visible build conditions because disabled contributors are still given a defined zero value.

conceptual assets.concept: Register-file write-back value delivered to the CPU register file
conceptual assets.reasoning: Line 330 computes rf_wdata as the bitwise OR of alu_res, lsu_rdata, csr_rdata and ctrl.pc_ret, and line 323 delivers rf_wdata to the register-file sub-unit as rd_i. Integrity is Established because the register-file consumer must receive exactly the write-back value defined by line 330; corruption would update architectural register state with the wrong data. Availability is also Established for the local combination itself because this wrapper continuously drives rf_wdata from the listed contributors.

conceptual assets.concept: PMP access-fault decision used by control and LSU
conceptual assets.reasoning: When PMP support is enabled, pmp_fault is driven from the PMP sub-unit output fault_o at line 420; when PMP support is disabled, line 427 forces pmp_fault to '0'. The resulting decision is consumed by control at line 257 and by LSU at line 392. Integrity is Established because both consumers must receive exactly the fault/no-fault decision defined by the active configuration; corrupting it changes whether the load/store path is treated as faulting. Availability is Established because the RTL provides a defined value in both configurations.
